introH2: ⛰️ What kinds of stays are near Khao Laem Ya National Park in Rayong, and how do you pick the right one?
introHtml: Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park is the heart of a beach trip on the Rayong coast — the viewpoints up on Khao Laem Ya, Mae Ramphueng Beach stretching for kilometres, and the Ban Phe pier where you catch the boat onward to Ko Samet in about 30 minutes. But a "stay near Khao Laem Ya" doesn't come in just one shape, and that's exactly what makes choosing here something to match to your trip. Some are small hotels where a two-minute walk gets you to Mae Ramphueng Beach for a few hundred baht; some are beach resorts perched on the tip of Laem Tan with a private beach and every room opening onto the sea; some are white-sand Bali-style boutique pool resorts; and some are quiet loft resorts tucked into a garden. A lot of people book somewhere by the sea without checking whether it's "on the beach" or "a walk to the beach," then arrive feeling it isn't what they pictured. This article rounds up 5 stays in Rayong's Khao Laem Ya–Mae Ramphueng–Ban Phe area that we've reviewed in depth — every one drawn from reading real guest reviews, telling you both the upsides and the honest caveats, compared across 3 sites, with full direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Rayong has no skytrain or dense public transit, so having your own car or calling a ride is by far the easiest way around, and all 5 stays in this article have free parking. From Bangkok it's about a 2–3 hour drive to this area via the motorway, and U-Tapao Airport (UTP) is about a 30–55 minute drive away. The areas in this article: Mae Ramphueng Beach · Taphong Subdistrict — a popular long sandy beach with hotels and resorts within walking distance or close to the sand, near Khao Laem Ya and the seafood restaurants along the shore. Laem Tan · Ban Phe — the tip of the cape adjoining Khao Laem Ya National Park, with a private beach, about 3 km from the Ban Phe pier to Ko Samet. The two areas are about a 15–20 minute drive apart and both work as a base before catching the boat to Ko Samet.

entries.type: 3-Star Beach Hotel · Walk to Mae Ramphueng Beach
entries.name: The Great Rayong Hotel
entries.badge: 🏖️ 2-min walk to the sea · best value
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Taphong · Mae Ramphueng Beach · 2-min walk to the sea
entries.addr: 77/9 Moo 5, Taphong Subdistrict, Mueang Rayong District
entries.storyHtml: If one stay around Khao Laem Ya fits the phrase "staying near the sea for a few hundred baht" most precisely, plenty of reviews give it to this one — The Great Rayong Hotel is a small 3-star hotel of about 42 rooms in the Mae Ramphueng Beach area, Taphong Subdistrict, Mueang Rayong District, whose main pitch is "close to the sea at a reachable price." It scores 8.5 from 151 reviews on Trip.com. What reviews mention most is that the hotel sits only about 650 metres from Mae Ramphueng Beach, roughly a 2-minute walk — wake up, step out a few paces, and you're on the sand by the sea, then drive on to Khao Laem Ya or the Ban Phe pier to cross to Ko Samet. Two more things draw repeated praise: the breakfast included in the room rate, which real reviews agree is "free and tasty" and more varied than the price suggests, and the free parking, which matters a lot since Rayong relies mainly on your own car. Rooms start with the Standard at about 23 sq.m., with King and Twin beds and a limited number of sea-view rooms to choose from, up to a Family Room at about 50 sq.m., and there's a decent-sized outdoor pool to cool off in after a beach run. Honest caveats from the reviews: the building is fairly aged and is being renovated room by room, so room condition can vary; some have a musty smell in the bathroom or cleanliness that isn't consistent across every room, and some furniture is starting to show its age. This isn't a luxe on-the-sand resort, but it's the best value per baht in this area for budget travellers, couples and small families on a simple beach trip, and anyone using Rayong as a one-night stop before Ko Samet.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a recently renovated room when you book or check in, since the hotel renovates room by room and conditions differ. If you want to wake up to the sea, request a sea-view room in advance because there are only a limited number, and make the most of the free breakfast before heading out to the beach.

entries.storyHtml: Among these 5 stays, if you go by review score, Rayong Resort Hotel is the top scorer at 8.7 from 268 reviews, and TripAdvisor ranks it #1 of 6 hotels in Phe Subdistrict. It's a 4-star beach resort set on the tip of Laem Tan, which juts out into the sea adjoining Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park, only about 0.5 km from the Khao Laem Ya viewpoint — which makes it a genuinely "next to the park" stay in this article. The charm reviews agree on is that almost every room has a private balcony looking out over the sea and the silhouette of Ko Samet — open the balcony door in the morning and Ban Phe Bay is right there. What gets talked about most is the private sandy beach on the tip and the fishing pier reaching about 380 metres out to sea, which has become a favourite photo and strolling spot at dawn and dusk, paired with three outdoor pools spread out so guests don't have to compete for space and kids can swim easily. There's also Daovadeung Spa, kayaking, and a conference centre for groups of up to about 500 for seminars. The Ban Phe pier is only about 3 km away, with a roughly 30-minute boat ride to Ko Samet, so it works well as a base before and after the island. Honest caveats: the resort has been open since 1988, so parts of the building and some rooms are aged and a few are fairly small; the location is private but remote; outside restaurants close early around 9 pm, so without a car going out in the evening is awkward; and it's a natural beach on Ban Phe Bay, so at certain times of year debris washes in with the tide. It suits families who want their kids to swim in the sea and pools to their hearts' content, couples after privacy by the beach, and anyone who values a sea view over how new the room is.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a high-floor Deluxe Sea View (floors 5–7) or a recently renovated room at booking, since standards vary quite a bit by zone and the view from up high helps offset the age. The location is fairly remote and outside restaurants close early, so if you don't have a car, plan to have dinner at the resort and ask about the shuttle to the Ban Phe pier in advance.

entries.name: Ohana Resort and Restaurant
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mae Ramphueng Beach · Taphong · 5–10 min walk to the beach
entries.addr: 45/7 Moo 10, Hat Mae Ramphueng–Sukhumvit Road, Taphong Subdistrict, Mueang Rayong District
entries.storyHtml: Among these 5 stays, if you go by the number of reviews, Ohana Resort and Restaurant has the most — about 369 reviews, scoring 8.6 on Trip.com and 8.5 on Booking.com. It's a small white-toned boutique resort with a clean look, decorated in a Bali-meets-modern style and surrounded by coconut palms, in the Mae Ramphueng Beach area of Taphong Subdistrict, near Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park. What every platform agrees on, and the real star, is the two pools — especially the white-sand seawater pool that mimics a beach: you can walk down and feel the sand underfoot like the real thing. And what thrills the kids is that there are fish and turtles swimming in the pool to feed — many families say this is the main reason they come back, because their children get to swim sea-style in a space that's safer and easier to supervise than an actual beach. Another much-discussed point is the variety of room styles, each decorated differently — some have an in-room jacuzzi like the Tidy Room, and the headline Canopy Room has a jacuzzi by the balcony plus a private rooftop for stargazing, which is romantic for couples. Breakfast is cooked to order à la carte, and some international reviewers even rate it the best breakfast they've ever had. The resort isn't directly on the beach, but it's about a 5–10 minute walk to Mae Ramphueng Beach, with bikes to borrow and free parking. Honest caveats: because it's not on the beach, most rooms have garden or pool views rather than full sea views; the dining options at the resort are limited and the restaurant isn't open for every meal; and some reviews note that a few spots are starting to age and pool cleanliness is inconsistent at times. It suits couples who want a romantic room with a jacuzzi, families who want their kids to swim safely in a seawater pool, and anyone after pretty photo spots with an overseas feel on a reachable budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want a jacuzzi, choose the Tidy Room (in-room tub); if you want a stargazing rooftop, choose the Canopy Room — and specify the room type clearly when you book, because the entry-level rooms may not have it. If you're travelling with kids, ask the resort about the feeding times for the fish and turtles in the seawater pool so you don't miss it, and plan to head out to the seafood restaurants around Mae Ramphueng Beach for lunch and dinner.

entries.name: Panwana Resort

entries.addr: 104/40 Moo 9, Soi Noen Klang 5, Taphong Subdistrict, Mueang Rayong District
entries.storyHtml: If the other stays in this article sell closeness to the sea, Panwana Resort chose to sell the opposite — quiet, and a homey feel. It's a very small loft-style boutique resort of just 11 rooms, tucked down Soi Noen Klang 5 in the Taphong area of Mueang Rayong District. It isn't on the beach, but it's about a 10-minute drive from here to Mae Ramphueng Beach and Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park. It scores about 8.4 "very good" on Agoda from a hundred-odd verified reviews, and 8.3 on Trip.com (with location rated 8.8). The selling point here isn't a sea view but the quiet garden atmosphere, shady coconut palms, a small stream running through, and the easy, welcoming feel of staying at a relative's place. The rooms are loft-style, with bare grey-and-black concrete walls set against warm-toned wood furniture for a raw but cosy look; the Signature is a two-storey room with a netting-hammock nook to lounge in. What sets Panwana apart from the usual small stay is the outdoor pool in the middle of the garden, which is unusual for an 11-room resort, and Pada Cafe, the on-site cafe decorated in a pink-and-green Bali style that bills itself as a matcha bar, serving several kinds of matcha, smoothies, and desserts at around ฿100–200 — wake up, walk a few steps, and sip your matcha by the pool. Real reviews especially highlight the service from the owner family — they speak English, they're kind, and they look after you like a guest in their home. Honest caveats: you really need your own car since the resort is down a lane, the entrance is fairly dark at night and there's no 24-hour staff, some reviews complain about insects on the bedding at times, and being a small stay, the food menu and services aren't as complete as a big hotel. It suits couples and small families who want a quiet stay on a budget, focused on the atmosphere and the cute cafe corner, then using it as a base while driving out to the beach and Ko Samet.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Book a Deluxe room on a weekday for the best rate, and because the resort is down a lane with a dark entrance at night, give your check-in time in advance and get the owner's contact number in case you arrive after dark. Drop by Pada Cafe in the morning before the crowds, and plan to use this as a quiet base while driving out to Mae Ramphueng Beach, Khao Laem Ya, and the Ban Phe pier.

entries.name: Sea Sand Sun Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mae Ramphueng Beach · Taphong · about 250 m from the beach
tags: 🍳 Roomy units with a small kitchen
🏖️ About 250 m walk to the beach
entries.addr: 182/111 Hat Mae Ramphueng Road, Taphong Subdistrict, Mueang Rayong District
entries.storyHtml: We close the article with an option for groups — Sea Sand Sun Resort at Mae Ramphueng Beach, a 3-star condotel-style resort whose pitch is "roomy units with a kitchen on a budget." Its overall score on Trip.com is about 8.2. The property sits on the Taphong Subdistrict side of Mueang Rayong District, built as several apartment-unit buildings rented out by the night, so the rooms are larger than a typical hotel room, and many have a small kitchenette with a balcony. The main location selling point is that it's only about 250 metres from Mae Ramphueng Beach, an easy walk — the property isn't right on the sand where you open the door to the beach, but a short walk across the road brings you to the long stretch of sand lined with seafood restaurants and sunset spots, and you can drive on to the Ban Phe pier to cross to Ko Samet in about 20–30 minutes. The highlight that draws the most consistent praise is the large outdoor pool, wide enough for kids and adults to swim at the same time, with garden space around it and a kids' pool zone at times. There's also a restaurant, Thai massage service, a tennis court, and free parking. Having a kitchen in the room lets many families buy from the market and cook for themselves, cutting food costs for a big group or a long trip — split among several people, the per-person nightly cost is very low. Honest caveats: the building is fairly aged (last major renovation around 2011), so some rooms and beds aren't new, cleanliness and service aren't as consistent as a chain hotel, the restaurant/bar service is inconsistent and some packages don't include breakfast, some reviews ran into mosquitoes, and parts of Mae Ramphueng Beach get debris blown and washed in by the wind and waves. It suits families with small kids, groups of friends travelling together, and anyone who wants to cook for themselves or stay several nights, who weigh space, a kitchen, and per-person price over how new and polished the place is.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose a Deluxe room with a kitchen, or one noted as recently renovated, because room condition here can vary quite a bit by building and renovation round. Check first whether the package you book includes breakfast (some rooms don't), in case you plan to eat at a beachside restaurant or cook in the room, and if you're sensitive to mosquitoes, bring repellent because the property is next to a garden and near the sea.

faqTitle: FAQ — common questions travellers ask about stays near Khao Laem Ya, Rayong

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best stay near Khao Laem Ya National Park in Rayong?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. If you go by score and being genuinely "next to the park," Rayong Resort Hotel scores 8.7, the highest in the article, sits on the tip of Laem Tan adjoining Khao Laem Ya about 0.5 km away, and has a private beach. If you go by number of reviews, Ohana Resort has the most, about 369, and stands out for its white-sand seawater pool. If you want to walk to the beach cheaply, The Great Rayong Hotel at ฿750 is a 2-minute walk from Mae Ramphueng Beach. If you want a quiet garden stay, Panwana Resort. And if you're a group wanting a room with a kitchen, Sea Sand Sun Resort.

faq.q: ❓ How much do stays near Khao Laem Ya, Rayong cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at about ฿750–3,000 per night. On the budget side, The Great Rayong starts at ฿750 and Sea Sand Sun at ฿900. Mid-range is Panwana at ฿1,200 and Ohana at ฿1,800. And at the beach-resort level is Rayong Resort Hotel from ฿3,000 (high-floor sea-view rooms up to about ฿4,500). All prices are approximate starting rates from standard rooms; over long weekends and the high season, prices can be higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in if I want to visit Khao Laem Ya and Ko Samet?
faq.a: Mae Ramphueng Beach · Taphong Subdistrict suits those who want to walk to a long sandy beach, near Khao Laem Ya and the seafood restaurants (The Great Rayong, Ohana, Sea Sand Sun). Laem Tan · Ban Phe suits those who want a private beach adjoining the park and to be near the pier to Ko Samet (Rayong Resort Hotel). And Taphong down a lane suits those who want a quiet garden stay, a 10-minute drive to the beach (Panwana Resort) — every area is within driving distance of the Ban Phe pier to catch the boat to Ko Samet.

faq.q: ❓ Which stays can you really walk to the beach from, and which aren't on the beach?
faq.a: Walk to the beach: The Great Rayong, about a 2-minute walk (~650 m) · Sea Sand Sun, about a 250-metre walk · Ohana, about a 5–10 minute walk. Private beach at the stay: Rayong Resort Hotel on the tip of Laem Tan has its own private beach. Not on the beach, need to drive: Panwana Resort is down a lane in the Taphong area, about a 10-minute drive to Mae Ramphueng Beach. If a sea view from your room is the main goal, Rayong Resort Hotel suits best because almost every room has a sea-view balcony.

faq.q: ❓ Which stay near Khao Laem Ya is good for families with kids?
faq.a: The standout is Ohana Resort, with its white-sand seawater pool with fish and turtles for kids to feed, safer than a real beach. Next is Rayong Resort Hotel, with 3 outdoor pools and a private beach where kids can swim to their hearts' content. And Sea Sand Sun Resort, with a large pool and roomy kitchen units, suits long family stays — all three have free parking for those driving themselves.

faq.q: ❓ How far in advance should I book a stay near Khao Laem Ya?
faq.a: Many of the stays in this article are small (Panwana just 11 rooms · The Great Rayong about 42 rooms), so they fill up fast. For long weekends, festivals and the seaside high season (Nov–Feb, plus weekends), book 2–4 weeks ahead or more, especially the popular Rayong Resort Hotel and Ohana Resort. For weekdays out of season, 1–2 weeks ahead is enough. Every platform usually offers Free Cancellation — it's worth locking in a rate like that if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
